_comment: Species deliberately kept OUT of the native-plant catalogue, with the reason and the authority for each. src/data_quality.py:validate_excluded_taxa fails the build if one reappears in data/plants_master.json, data/garden_plants.json or as the `plant` of an edge in data/plant_fauna_master.json.
_why_this_file_exists: A plant is removed once and can come back many times. Rudbeckia hirta shipped flagged `native_to_alberta = 1` and noted 'Classic prairie wildflower', so nothing in the app disagreed with it — and data/fetched/fauna_edges_candidates.json still holds 389 GloBI records naming it, ready to be re-proposed by the next sourcing pass. A deletion with no record of the decision is an invitation to redo it.
_scope: This is NOT a nativity gate. It is a list of specific calls that were made, each with its evidence. A species absent from the catalogue and absent from here has simply never been considered.
_p9: `authority` names who says so. Where the authorities disagree the entry says so rather than picking one silently — see docs/DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md P9.

taxa.authority: VASCAN (Database of Vascular Plants of Canada) records Rudbeckia hirta as introduced in AB, SK, MB and BC, and native from Ontario eastward. Moss, Flora of Alberta, agrees: introduced. It is a garden and wildflower-mix escape here, not a member of any Alberta plant community.
taxa.disagreement: Occurrence data does not settle this and should not be read as if it did — the plant_ecoregions entry removed with this row carried 215 georeferenced GBIF records across eight prairie ecoregions, 102 of them in Aspen Parkland. That is what a widely-planted self-seeder looks like. Presence is not nativity; see src/establishment.py.
taxa.took_with_it: 150 documented plant-fauna edges, 1 plant_ecoregions entry, 2 seeded polyculture memberships and 1 worked-example fallback.
taxa.substitute: Ratibida columnifera (Prairie Coneflower) — the native yellow-rayed, dark-coned composite it was standing in for, at a similar height and bloom window.
